# Wiki Compilation Goals

> Curated section: Overview.

> Keep the knowledge base as executable rules for CAFES.

## Rule

- Prefer canonical rule pages over repeated explanatory prose.
- Each page must name the trigger, required action, forbidden action, validation gate, and failure pattern when applicable.
- When a rule conflicts with a descriptive note, the rule wins.

## Must

- Use short imperative language: must, must not, reject, normalize, require approval.
- Keep aliases in frontmatter rather than as visible folded-topic prose.
- Use tables or bullet lists for contracts, fields, operation vocabularies, and approval matrices.

## Must Not

- Do not keep duplicate rule bodies across pages.
- Do not create dangling wiki links to pages that are not generated.
- Do not expose raw chain-of-thought or hidden planner JSON as user-facing knowledge.

# Wiki Maintenance Rules

> Curated section: Overview.

> Conversation-derived rules enter the main wiki only after promotion into maintained source files.

## Rule Inbox

- Capture conversation-derived rules in conversation_rules first.
- Promote stable rules into sources during periodic maintenance.
- Keep rough, contradictory, or unreviewed notes out of sources.

## Promotion Checklist

- Decide whether the rule belongs in an existing source or a new source file.
- Preserve the rationale or failure case when it explains why the rule exists.
- Add related-page links and curated-structure entries when needed.
- If a source changes runtime behavior, make sure code and tests enforce it.
- Run the wiki curate/lint flow after source updates.

## Must Not

- Do not assume conversation_rules are available to the planner at runtime.
- Do not edit generated wiki pages as the source of truth.
- Do not let generated capability tables drift away from the runtime registry.

## Publication And Retrieval

- Maintained sources outrank historical compiler candidates and exports. pageGuidance is an explicit body override: revise it together with its source, then run wiki:curate and wiki:lint.
- Use English guidance. Verify bounded retrieved passages from the packaged runtime export for changed scientific topics; do not send the whole Wiki or Registry to the LLM.
- Keep executable Registry facts, heuristic interpretation, future proposals, and completed numerical evidence distinct. Runtime retrieval reads the packaged export on each call; only Python code changes require a service reload.

pages.title: CAFES Architecture
pages.summary: Defines the global system boundary between planning, execution, solver selection, state, artifacts, and approval gates.
pages.body:
# CAFES Architecture

> Curated section: Overview.

> Defines the global system boundary between planning, execution, solver selection, state, artifacts, and approval gates.

## System Layers

- Planner layer decomposes user goals into approved cases.
- Execution graph layer runs one normalized task specification at a time.
- Molecular-correlation and model-Hamiltonian subpackages implement diagnostics and solver-specific behavior.
- Solver layer maps validated molecular methods or model-Hamiltonian solvers to PySCF calls.
- State/artifact layer keeps compact execution state separate from persisted files.
- Approval layer separates conversation, plan construction, calculation execution, active-space review, and recovery review.
- Application-service layer exposes the same task and study use cases to Web, CLI, local, and remote adapters.
- Execution-target layer selects local or named Slurm infrastructure without changing the scientific task specification.
- Web presentation uses small HTML shells, responsibility-scoped JavaScript/CSS package assets, and one shared molecular-preview implementation.
- Task orchestration executes registered modules; study orchestration owns complete tasks, approvals, dependencies, cross-case analysis, refinement, and the merged report.
- Molecular datasets reuse Study and Task: one trajectory per seed molecule, sampled AO matrices in artifacts, and separate dataset finalization, generation, and collection.
- Web LocalProcessExecutor persists verified process identities and supports cancellation after restart. An independent POSIX supervisor enforces optional wall_time_seconds; the termination grace period is separate. Setting the local wall-time CLI flag also selects supervised execution for synchronous callers.
- Optional immutable remote releases bind a local source fingerprint to the server runtime; deployment identity is execution infrastructure, not a scientific TaskSpec field.

## Must

- Execute only normalized task specifications.
- Keep solver choice, charge, spin, reference, and method selection in the task-spec/execution layer.
- Keep generated input files, logs, spectra, and structured results in run-directory artifacts.
- Require approval gates before planner-generated execution.
- Treat an MP2 active-space probe as a registered preparation role and preserve the requested CAS method, target solver, and solver options for the approved task.
- Use one authoritative study lifecycle; derive presentation actions from it instead of maintaining competing workflow stages.
- Rebuild the complete StudyReport from current saved Task/Run results in the backend; browser session state is only a view cache.
- Keep server and resource-profile selection in execution metadata; servers own their queue, CPU, memory, and wall-time values.
- Serve Assistant and Planner static assets from package resources and keep HTML, CSS, and JavaScript in package-data manifests.

## Must Not

- Do not treat chat history as executable state.
- Do not let UI defaults silently override the structured task specification.
- Do not make a UI surface responsible for backend validation.
- Do not infer study review type from special study ids, private plan keys, UI modes, or conversation text.

## Current Migration Boundary

- Study -> Task -> Run ownership and full-report merging across selected retries are implemented. New checkpoints store TaskReport references and compact status summaries; existing inline checkpoints remain readable.
- Specialized scientific stages retain procedural adapters, and some review services transport a parent report and private stage fields. Typed review/stage adapters may improve these boundaries independently; a report-revision engine is not required for ordinary retries.
- Task module handlers must return a dictionary, but completed traces record declared output names without validating every realized output port schema.

pages.title: Design Philosophy And Layer Boundaries
pages.summary: Keep scientific intent, executable facts, lifecycle control, numerical execution, and persisted evidence under separate authorities.
pages.body:
# Design Philosophy And Layer Boundaries

> Curated section: Architecture.

> Keep scientific intent, executable facts, lifecycle control, numerical execution, and persisted evidence under separate authorities.

## Public Boundary

- Package roots expose application services and task/study contracts, not workflow steps, executors, provider adapters, or compatibility facades.
- Web, CLI, local Python, remote RPC, and MCP call the same protocol-neutral application services. MCP lets Codex invoke the existing agent; it must not duplicate static/adaptive sequencing, scientific policy, recovery or result merging.
- TaskSpec/TaskReport describe one calculation; StudySpec/StudyPlan/StudyReport describe relationships among complete tasks.

## Authority

- PlatformRegistry defines executable capabilities, modules, gates, providers, bindings, parameters, observables, and artifacts.
- The LLM Wiki explains scientific policy and limitations but cannot enable execution; the UI owns presentation but cannot override validation.
- State machines own lifecycle and approval; reports own structured outcomes; artifacts own large numerical evidence and provenance.

## Composition

- A module owns a reusable step, a capability belongs to a module, a provider supplies an implementation boundary, and a binding selects its runtime adapter.
- Construct workflows top-down from requested capabilities and verify them bottom-up through module inputs, provider bindings, gates, and declared outputs.
- Keep inseparable upstream self-consistent loops as composite provider modules instead of inventing unsupported intermediate APIs.

## Scientific Control

- The LLM may interpret requests and explain structured evidence; deterministic contracts, validation, gates, and providers control execution.
- Initial study cases remain independent unless a dependency is declared; cross-case continuation and method promotion occur only in explicit analysis or refinement stages.
- Use general diagnostics and registered evidence rather than benchmark-specific branches or molecule-specific thresholds.
- The LLM owns free-text interpretation. Transport adapters must preserve its complete structured revision; they must not override scientific choices through keyword matching, inferred scan identities, or seed reconstruction.
- Missing diagnostics are unavailable evidence, not a weak-correlation classification. Optional artifact failures retain valid numerical results but record the missing evidence and failure reason.
- The backend owns executable review and recovery actions. Browser presentation must not invent actions absent from the workflow report.

## Dependency Direction

- The intended direction is public API to application services to contracts and registry to workflow runtime to providers and executors.
- Extend the existing authority for a concern; do not add a second catalog, result format, workflow state, or compatibility facade.
- Persist normalized inputs, generated PySCF scripts, logs, checkpoints, arrays, and plot data as registered evidence for reproducibility.

## Scientific Input And Evidence Boundaries

- The LLM returns explicit basis and coordinate proposals; request preparation does not authorize scientific defaults from keywords or summaries. Without an interpreter, an unapplied natural-language edit is unavailable, not ready.
- Repeated adaptive normalization preserves request identity and sparse explicit provider choices. Shared owner contracts reject lossy integers, malformed options and invalid booleans; browser controls cannot replace filled invalid values with defaults.
- Unknown classifications block routing. Missing UNO evidence is not zero fractionality. Nonphysical model occupations retain raw values and out_of_bounds status. Optional evidence generation records failure reasons while preserving completed energies.
- Root assignment retains an exact best/runner-up ambiguity margin for every root count. Spin-free entropy fallback requires a verified SU(2) singlet; unavailable NPDM evidence on other spin sectors cannot justify that substitution.

# Three-Surface Separation Architecture

> Curated section: Architecture.

> Builder, single-calculation agent, and planner are separate UI/interaction surfaces with explicit handoffs.

## Surfaces

- Builder surface edits model-Hamiltonian geometry, parameters, boundary conditions, and saved input artifacts.
- Single-calculation surface prepares and runs one molecular, periodic, or model-Hamiltonian task.
- Planner surface turns a broader scientific request into approved cases that reuse single-calculation workflows.

## Handoff Contract

- Builder to agent/planner handoff is a saved input path plus target identifier.
- Planner to single-calculation handoff is a normalized case task spec.
- Single-calculation to planner handoff is structured results plus artifact paths.
- Use target identifiers when the builder returns data to another surface.
- Preserve each surface's state across navigation.

## Must Not

- Do not couple builder UI state to solver execution state.
- Do not infer solver choice from builder UI state.
- Do not refresh the caller page when returning from builder navigation.
- Do not reuse hidden UI state as scientific input.

# Predefined Workflow Architecture

> Curated section: Architecture.

> The LLM proposes; the backend validates and executes through fixed workflow gates.

## Rule

- LLM may propose a task, edit a plan, or explain results.
- Backend must normalize and validate before execution.
- Tool selection is constrained by capability registries.
- Prior context is not executable truth.
- Expensive or risky steps require explicit user approval.

## Validation

- Reject unsupported methods, solvers, operations, or malformed electron counts.
- Normalize scalar total electron requests into spin-resolved electron counts before execution.
- Revalidate stale plans if input files, work directory, system type, or solver settings change.

## Failure Example

- A planner proposes `nelec: 3`; backend must convert or reject before running.
- A user asks for Hartree-Fock but stale DFT defaults remain in UI state; backend must execute the normalized spec, not the stale default.

# Capability Registry

> Curated section: Architecture.

> Planner freedom is bounded by registered runtime capabilities.

## Rule

- Every planner operation must correspond to a registered backend operation.
- Every solver choice must correspond to a registered solver capability.
- Unsupported actions are rejected or converted into a user-facing clarification.
- Capability status must distinguish executable, design-only, planned, and reference-only features.

## Must

- Use the registry to validate operation names, argument shapes, supported methods, supported solvers, and postprocessing tools.
- Derive study modes and adaptive initial-scan option ids from the Registry; serialize only canonical ids `auto`, `mp2`, and `fci`, with one method per full-grid initial plan.
- Validate every emitted artifact kind and JSON payload schema against `artifact_contracts`, including the dynamic `observable-*` pattern.
- Report validation failures before execution.
- Keep human approval after plan building and before run submission.
- Use audit tests to detect drift between registry facts, backend constants, planner operations, UI option ids, and generated capability exports.

## Must Not

- Do not treat wiki text or PySCF reference coverage as execution support.
- Do not put UI display labels, button text, layout, or helper copy into registry metadata.
- Do not edit generated capability markdown by hand; regenerate it from the runtime registry.

pages.body:
# Capability Registry Runtime Boundary

> Curated section: Architecture.

> The registry owns executable capability facts and flow semantics, not presentation details.

## Owns

- Capability family and canonical id.
- Execution status: executable, design_only, planned, or reference_only.
- Planner and backend allow flags.
- Runtime limitations that affect validation or planning.
- Calculation-flow semantics such as model-Hamiltonian parameter scopes: site, bond, global, and sweep.
- Registered workflow modules and roles, including active-space probes that prepare evidence without activating a target solver.
- Canonical study modes, adaptive initial-scan strategies and aliases, workflow options, artifact kinds/patterns, payload schemas, execution-target capabilities, public resource-profile ids, and cross-module resource limits.

## Does Not Own

- UI labels, layout, colors, button text, or helper copy.
- Long scientific explanations that belong in wiki source pages.
- Generated capability tables that can be recreated from code.
- Private SSH credentials and raw server queue, CPU, memory, or wall-time values.
- Browser-only UI state or test fixtures.

## Boundary Rule

- Backend constants and planner capability snapshots derive from the registry.
- UI adapters may derive option ids from the registry but own display labels.
- Wiki pages may explain rationale and roadmap, but runtime code must not depend on compiled wiki output to decide executability.
- Registry metadata must stay runtime-oriented; reject presentation-only keys such as ui_label.
- Probe modules identify their probe method and preserve target method, solver, and solver options in a structured contract.
- Calculation Assistant active-space selection always uses the canonical auto probe; only the Planner exposes auto, mp2, and fci initial-scan strategies.
- Serialize canonical adaptive ids `auto`, `mp2`, and `fci`; reject removed strategy ids and legacy solver fields instead of changing workflow semantics.
- Artifact audit tests must ensure every writer kind or dynamic pattern is registered and every declared payload schema is actually written.

# Workflow State Design Principles

> Curated section: Architecture.

> State is compact, structured, and separate from large artifacts.

## Must

- Store artifact paths instead of large stdout, spectra, or full generated code in workflow state.
- Store compact summaries and structured result keys for LLM-visible context.
- Version state schemas when adding new task families or result formats.
- Persist `pyscf-agent.study-plan.v1`, `study-state.v1`, `study-report.v1`, and adaptive workflow/report schemas instead of relying on chat history.

## Must Not

- Do not duplicate long stdout and parsed summaries in multiple state fields.
- Do not rely on implicit defaults that are absent from serialized state.
- Do not allow hidden state to diverge from the user-visible form.

## Study Resume And Retry

- Status and Collect never create an attempt. Run may retry within its existing approval and bounds; recovering persisted handles retains the current attempt.
- Keep execution associations in the existing checkpoint rather than adding another retry workflow. Persist intent before submission and report unknown acknowledgement explicitly.
- Invalid checkpoints and missing new-format associations are errors, not empty state. Adopt compatible legacy receipts conservatively without submitting jobs.

# Public Data Contracts

> Curated section: Architecture.

> All application surfaces exchange the same versioned task, study, scheduler, and artifact structures.

## MCP Adapter

- The optional stdio MCP server exposes single-task validation, submission, status, collection and cancellation through CalculationApplicationService, using existing TaskSpec, JobHandle, JobStatus and TaskReport contracts.
- Task monitoring uses CalculationApplicationService.inspect_task: the Web view and MCP show_task/app-only refresh_task_view read the same executor status, saved report summary and bounded log evidence. Automatic refresh makes no LLM calls, never collects or executes, and stops at terminal status. Solver metrics are last observed evidence, not final task energies or convergence decisions. open_task_monitor retains the exact JobHandle; SSH inspection requires the updated remote inspect-task RPC. Inline rendering depends on the host.
- collect_task returns a named summary projection and full-report resource URI. Only the complete report carries the TaskReport schema; encoded handle references add no new task identity or persisted store.
- Registry and packaged wiki resources retain separate authority. Scientific approval gates and convergence retries remain runtime-owned; MCP validation does not grant approval.
- Study tools save static/adaptive preparation and start one background call to the existing agent runner. submit_study maps to application start_study; the per-task submit-only path is removed. Study ID survives client exit. Existing plans, checkpoints, reports and receipts remain authoritative. study-invocation.json and its inherited POSIX lock record only the latest application process, not another task state machine. Review decisions are saved in StudyReport.pending_review and require explicit start by Study ID; collection never submits work.
- analyze_study calls deterministic agent diagnostics without an LLM or new calculations; existing MPS/path approvals start those services separately. prepare_dataset calls the existing dataset planner, Task validation and ordinary Study runner, exposing its accepted/rejected sample manifest. No protocol-owned scientific execution is added.

## Stable Structures

- TaskSpec is the validated request passed to one executor and TaskReport is its scientific result.
- StudySpec defines a multi-case objective, StudyPlan expands executable cases, and StudyReport is the authoritative merged study record.
- JobHandle and JobStatus describe scheduler identity and lifecycle without replacing scientific status.
- Artifact references carry kind, path, size_bytes, mime_type, and description; registered JSON artifacts carry their own versioned schemas. Full initial_mo_coeff matrices use pyscf-agent.numeric-array.v1 NPY references with shape and dtype; only numerical consumers load arrays. Long presentation text stays in artifacts with bounded previews. JSON writes stream into atomic temporary files.
- HamiltonianDatasetSpec, HamiltonianSample, rejection, and manifest contracts live in computational_study_agent.datasets.hamiltonian.contracts; StudyReport has a dataset_manifest field.
- RuntimeIdentity describes the deployed source and public contract; large numerical arrays stay in registered artifacts.

## Retry Persistence Compatibility

- The existing study checkpoint gains execution_associations_version=1 and case execution associations containing run_id, receipt_path, pending, and the outer attempt number. Case dictionaries preserve these fields in StudyReport round trips.
- Execution receipts record submission_unknown before handles are acknowledged. Explicit reconcile_execution verifies server-owned submission.json evidence against request fingerprints, case IDs, pending run IDs, and receipt ownership before restoring handles. Reconciliation never submits work; missing or partial evidence remains unknown.
- Collect is an application-service operation without submission side effects. A subsequent conversion fix now also preserves top-level StudyReport extensions.

## Contract Ownership

- pyscf_agent.contracts owns TaskSpec, TaskReport, and task serialization helpers.
- pyscf_agent.schema_contracts owns public schema identifiers, compatibility policy, and envelope validation; computational_study_agent.schema owns study dataclasses.
- An LLM prompt, UI payload, scheduler record, or process-local PySCF object is never a public scientific contract.

## Public API

- pyscf_agent exposes CalculationApplicationService, TaskSpec, TaskReport, PlatformRegistry, and default_registry.
- computational_study_agent exposes StudyApplicationService, StudySpec, StudyPlan, StudyCase, and StudyReport.
- Executors and registry contracts remain in focused namespaces; workflow nodes, parsers, runners, retry helpers, provider adapters, and catalog builders remain internal.
- Do not recreate the removed pyscf_agent_backend or backend.models compatibility facades.

## Boundary Rules

- Readers accept additive fields and must preserve them during read-write round trips.
- Do not expose process-local PySCF objects; persist numerical arrays and pass registered artifact references.
- Do not use a free-form dictionary as a second public TaskReport or StudyReport format.
- Run and Collect return complete reports from current task checkpoints. Review subsets retain the original Study ID, and collection can load the saved plan by ID without a browser report.

## Report Compatibility And Remaining Migration

- StudyReport declares optional adaptive/postprocessing objects and preserves other accepted additive fields at their original top-level keys. Input, object, and exported nested values are independent copies.
- The reader accepts base study-report.v1, existing adaptive-study-report.v1, and schema-less legacy base reports. Output preserves the input schema; schema-less input receives base v1. Missing optional extensions default to null, and empty objects remain empty.
- Incompatible schemas and malformed known extensions are rejected; adaptive-schema input requires an adaptive object. Use to_dict() for serialization, not dataclasses.asdict().
- The adaptive runner still returns its versioned dictionary. Preserving evidence fixes the former data-loss boundary; typed stage adapters and review context remain possible improvements. Ordinary retries merge current Task/Run outcomes without a report-revision engine.

## Optional Evidence Status

- Reference 1RDM capture failures appear in evidence_errors; CAS natural_occupation_evidence and t2_orbital_importance_evidence expose status and reasons. Successful numerical energies survive optional evidence-generation failures.
- Model natural_occupation_summary preserves raw occupations and reports out_of_bounds beyond numerical roundoff, with null fractionality metrics. Consumers exclude unavailable/invalid evidence from scoring instead of interpreting it as weak correlation.

pages.body:
# Study Orchestration And Report Authority

> Curated section: Architecture.

> Explains Study -> Task -> Run ownership, complete report updates, recoverable execution, and the remaining specialized-stage boundary.

## Study, Task, And Run

- A Study owns tasks (cases), and each task identifies its current run and attempt count. Approved review subsets retain Study and case IDs; retries create distinct run directories. Batch handles and receipts group submissions without a child Study.
- The September 6 correction removes child registration, exported task-to-child references, and the separate integrate_review_execution API. Run and Collect return the complete StudyReport.

## Persisted Responsibilities

- study-plan.json retains the complete task set and latest task contracts. study-state.json owns current runs, receipts, attempt counts, task_report_ref pointers, compact task_summary status, and lifecycle. Collected TaskReports live in case-reports and are written before the checkpoint. Status reads do not load reports or arrays; collection explicitly reads report JSON. Legacy inline checkpoints remain readable without changing submitted input fingerprints. Optional review metadata records scientific stage kind and selected cases without execution ownership.
- Receipts own scheduler batches or local case-to-JobHandle associations and transport status; TaskReports own scientific outcomes; StudyReport owns comparisons, analysis, and artifacts. Browser snapshots cannot replace current checkpoint results. No additional state framework or report revision system is required.

## Execution And Recovery

- Run executes an approved subset or explicit case/status selection while retaining unselected task results and contracts. It first recovers pending executions across the same Study rather than replaying a submission.
- Background Start invokes existing run_study/run_adaptive_study once through completion, required review or interruption. The runner owns sequencing; MCP clients do not advance tasks manually. Invocation metadata and a POSIX lock identify the coordinator across client exits without replacing task state.
- MCP Study tools call application services by saved Study ID. Direct-CAS preparation and probe review are shared with Web. Review saves its decision in StudyReport.pending_review for explicit start by Study ID; it never executes the decision itself.
- Collect loads saved input and current handles without submitting failed or unstarted tasks. can_collect is false while the agent runs; scientific success is determined from StudyReport. An interrupted adaptive collection may prepare a stage which needs a later explicit Run.
- Remote Collect and direct execution share complete-batch acceptance before checkpoint updates. Missing or extra cases and mismatched run identities cannot partially complete a batch. Unknown submissions require existing server evidence, not another submission.

## Report Updates

- Run/Collect rebuild the full comparison from current TaskReports, preserving unselected results, existing observables, unchanged annotations, and adaptive/postprocessing extensions. Scientific stage snapshots remain evidence within the same Study.
- Final success requires successful current results for every task. Reports are atomically written after task results; same-process Run/Collect operations share the Study lock. Background start/review/collect share an inherited process lock across MCP servers; direct Python/Web Run should not overlap that writer.

## Historical Data And Scope

- Completed legacy child/stage records can be imported from saved checkpoints into the original Study checkpoint without submitting calculations or moving artifacts. Pending historical child execution must be collected before migration. Browser-only numerical reports cannot seed execution state.
- Specialized initial/refined adaptive stages, MPS continuation, and bidirectional candidate evaluation retain their scientific orchestration and stage artifacts. This correction does not introduce a universal typed stage engine or a revision protocol.

# Planner Agent Approval Boundary

> Curated section: Planner.

> Plan construction and plan execution are separate approval gates.

## Rule

- Build plan approval allows the planner to create a concrete case table.
- Run approval allows the backend to execute approved cases.
- Run Plan performs independent case calculations; cross-case continuity checks and AO 1RDM reuse begin only after the user selects Analyze Results.
- Compatible block2 MPS reuse also begins only after Analyze Results and a fingerprinted continuation approval.
- Any task-changing edit after approval invalidates the approved plan.
- Active-space and recovery approvals apply to the selected case subset, not every failed case.

## Must

- Show the user the planned cases, changed parameters, solver/method, expected outputs, and work directory before run approval.

- Require re-approval after stale-plan detection.
- After a recovery subset completes, merge it into the parent report before showing further review or analysis.
- Show a CAS candidate's deterministic resource estimate in the same ActiveSpaceAudit review; cost acknowledgement does not replace scientific active-space approval.

## Must Not

- Do not start a calculation from a conversation send action.
- Do not treat a planning draft as execution approval.
- Do not hide case changes inside natural-language summaries.

# Planner Workflow Validation

> Curated section: Planner.

> Planner output must be checked, repaired, normalized, or rejected before it can enter execution.

## Validate Plan Structure

- Every plan must contain explicit cases or a deterministic rule for generating cases.
- Every case must map to one single-calculation task specification.
- Every operation must have a registered operation name and typed arguments.
- Every case must declare the input artifact it mutates or reuses.

## Registry Checks

- Validate operation names against the capability registry.
- Validate solver and method names against solver/method support.
- Validate site indices, bond indices, electron counts, unit fields, and artifact paths.
- Reject operations that require backend capabilities not yet implemented.
- Static model scans preserve unchanged sites, bonds, nelec, boundary, and unit metadata from the base input.
- Recovery subsets must preserve parent case identifiers and may mutate only the reviewed case.
- For adaptive molecular studies, run the registered initial method over the full grid, preserve case identity, and select further methods only in reviewed refinement or recovery. Model studies retain an explicit solver and can opt into parameter-grid refinement; see [[Model Grid Convergence Barriers]].

## Stale-Plan Checks

- Invalidate a plan when the base input file, work directory, model parameters, method, solver, charge, spin, nelec, or operation list changes.
- Require renewed plan approval after stale-plan detection.
- Do not run a stale case table even if a previous run approval exists.

## Repair / Normalize / Reject Policy

- Normalize scalar total electron requests into spin-resolved `nelec` when the rule is unambiguous.
- Repair harmless aliases such as method labels only when they map to one canonical backend value.
- Reject ambiguous, unsupported, or lossy transformations and return a user-facing issue.
- Accept the complete structured StudySpec returned by the Planner, including simultaneous global and case-local changes. Preserve explicit study mode and nested impurity-solver ownership; unsupported choices remain validation errors.
- Expand explicit start/stop/step case-variable ranges in the shared StudySpec contract. Reject malformed or excessive ranges rather than truncating them or guessing which model parameter they represent.

## Must Not

- Do not silently drop rejected operations.
- Do not run a partially invalid plan unless the user explicitly approves the reduced plan.
- Do not let LLM-generated scalar `nelec` reach execution.

## Failure Example

- `change_nelec` with a scalar value is invalid at execution boundary; normalize to `[nalpha, nbeta]` or reject with a repair instruction.

# Adaptive Scan Workflow State Machine

> Curated section: Planner.

> Adaptive scans use a versioned state machine so initial scan, approval, recovery, and full-report merge cannot be inferred only from chat history.

## States

- This method-routing state machine applies to adaptive molecular studies. Model studies retain an explicit solver under study_mode=static; optional grid_refinement changes sampling and has its own convergence barriers. Do not invent molecular initial-scan or active-space stages for model studies.
- Use `pyscf-agent.adaptive-workflow.v1` with execution states such as `initial_plan_ready`, `cost_review_required`, `initial_scan_blocked`, `active_space_review_required`, `recovery_review_required`, `completed`, and `completed_with_issues`, plus analysis-triggered MPS-continuation, AO-1RDM-continuation, and path-refinement review states.
- Keep full study plans distinct from refined and recovery subsets.
- Cost review is tied to a deterministic plan estimate; active-space review remains a separate scientific approval even when both appear in one review surface.
- Normal adaptive execution stores independent case results and a deferred path-analysis marker; it cannot enter continuation or path-refinement states before an explicit Analyze Results request.
- For unresolved block2 cases, Analyze Results checks compatible same-executor MPS continuation first; approved retries run sequentially and merge into the parent report.

## Review Modes

- For unresolved or blocked cases, set `review_mode=case_queue` and expose only `current_case_id` actions.
- For all ActiveSpaceAudit candidates in one executable refined, recovery, or path-refinement plan, set `review_mode=batch` and present their CAS evidence together.
- Advance a failed-case queue only after rebuilding workflow state from the merged parent report.
- Do not replay an approval request for a case that has already succeeded.
- Offer case-specific actions such as CASSCF promotion, active-space expansion, bounded max-cycle increase, guarded FCI, or blocked-input guidance instead of a generic plan-table review.

## Must Not

- Do not batch-approve non-equivalent failed cases.
- Do not replace a full adaptive report with one recovery result.
- Do not use conversation text as the recovery-state authority.

# Scan Path Continuity Diagnostics

> Curated section: Planner.

> Scan-path continuity is an explicit result-analysis capability; Run Plan leaves case calculations independent.

## Detection Rule

- Run the check only after the user selects Analyze Results; do not inspect neighboring cases or reuse their density matrices during normal adaptive execution.
- Apply only to completed one-dimensional scans with at least four successful energy points and exactly one numeric scan coordinate.
- Flag a boundary only when adjacent points use different methods and the transition slope disagrees with neighboring same-method slopes beyond both a relative and energy-residual threshold.
- Check one-sided endpoint risks separately and treat every finding as a numerical-routing quality signal, not a thermodynamic phase classifier or proof that a single-point diagnostic is wrong.

## Refinement Rule

- First retry the flagged local window in both coordinate directions without changing target methods, using compatible AO 1RDM artifacts from adjacent tasks.
- Require explicit review for endpoint validation and cross-method or cross-reference seeds; accept replacement results only when both branches converge and agree.
- Promote the overlap window to CASSCF only when continuation cannot establish a consistent branch.
- Create a separate plan-scoped ActiveSpaceAudit batch for the affected overlap region; do not silently run the promoted calculation.
- Merge approved local results back into the parent adaptive report before plotting or interpreting the full curve.

## Artifact Rule

- Normal adaptive execution writes `scan-path-diagnostics.json` with status `deferred` and schema `pyscf-agent.scan-path-diagnostics.v1`.
- After explicit analysis, store diagnostics, paired continuation plans and validation when used, or an `adaptive-path-refinement-plan` when method promotion is needed.

# Planner Agent Postprocessing

> Curated section: Planner.

> Registered Study postprocessing provides plots, exact plotted data, dataset exports and energy-stratified trajectory geometry selection.

## Built-In Tools

- `line_plot`, `scatter_plot`, `bar_plot`, and `heatmap` are the current built-in postprocessing tools.
- Supported postprocessing tool ids are runtime capabilities and should derive from the capability registry.
- Tool labels and UI presentation stay in UI adapters.

## Dataset Actions

- generate_hamiltonian_dataset and collect_hamiltonian_dataset are separate registered postprocessing actions, not plot tools; see [[Molecular Hamiltonian Dataset Workflow]].
- Finalization creates lightweight sample/rejection indexes without downloading remote NPZ files. Generation materializes and validates a portable dataset on the selected execution target and returns a receipt.
- Collection requires successful generation and transfers the already generated dataset only when requested. Neither action requires content-checksum validation.
- Derive trajectory/sample progress and generated/collected states from existing Study plans, receipts, and manifests rather than adding another scheduler state.

## Energy-Stratified Trajectory Selection

- Use registered postprocessing.action select_energy_stratified_frames to choose a labeling subset from accepted MD trajectories. It is owned by study.postprocessing and runs through the existing Study postprocessing API; the WebUI exposes Select by Energy.
- Pass count_per_molecule (required), time_start_fs (default 0), and time_end_fs (default null) in the action object. Each molecule is filtered by the inclusive time window, sorted by potential energy then frame index and sample ID, divided into equal-population energy bins (larger bins first), and represented by the lower median frame of each bin.
- Read only the accepted sample JSONL index, retaining geometry, energy, split and provenance; never load trajectory Fock/overlap arrays or call an LLM. The index must be accessible where postprocessing runs. Use provenance.time_au or the declared fixed MD timestep times frame_index for physical time.
- HamiltonianSample.total_energy_hartree means MD potential energy, not potential plus nuclear kinetic energy. Export registered selection-manifest JSON, selected-frames JSONL and Angstrom XYZ with source identities. Original trajectories and dataset splits remain unchanged; no CCSD is submitted.
- If a molecule has fewer candidates than requested, record the shortage and select none for it. Preserve visibility of source rejections and missing molecules; do not duplicate frames or claim a complete campaign. A time cutoff is an explicit sampling choice, not proof of equilibration; the selected frames are not guaranteed independent.

## Plot Rules

- Use matplotlib and a consistent publication-oriented style.
- Plot specs use comparison-table columns, not hardcoded domain names.
- Users must be able to choose x and y fields from available case variables and numeric result columns.
- For model Hamiltonian studies, numeric result columns may include final_energy, correlation_energy, filling, gap, mean_field_gap, natural_occupation_fractionality, fractional_natural_orbital_count, and max_double_excitation_amplitude when present.
- Each generated plot writes `plot-<name>.png`, `.spec.json`, `.data.tsv`, and `.data.json` under a shared prefix.
- Expose plotted TSV/JSON data with the figure; do not surface plot-spec JSON as the sole primary artifact.
- Plot only the merged full adaptive report, not an isolated recovery subset.
- Built-in plots exclude rows with publication_eligible=false and report excluded_case_ids; preserve the original rows and their quality evidence for review. An all-ineligible report skips plotting, while explicit dataset actions keep their separate eligibility checks.
- Plot artifacts use the common kind/path/size/MIME/description reference contract, and JSON spec/data payloads carry registered schemas.
- PostprocessContext owns eligible rows and column choices; WebUI consumes that projection. Explicit failed statuses exclude legacy rows with missing publication flags.
- Use cell or actual TaskSpec units; leave unknown units unlabeled and reject mixed/partly unknown units. Do not silently convert or relabel values.
- Validate explicit plot fields, group columns, positive integer DPI, finite figure sizes and heatmap center before rendering. Selected outputs must have distinct names.
- Render and export the same numeric rows; retain excluded case ids and reasons for missing numeric/group values in response and data JSON.

## Result Analysis Boundary

- Run Plan produces independent case results and records scan-path analysis as deferred.
- Analyze Results explicitly compares cases, runs path-continuity diagnostics, and may offer a reviewed 1RDM continuation or local method-refinement plan.
- Do not launch cross-case calculations merely because an adaptive run completed.
- Optional language analysis sends only contracts for actual result fields/artifact kinds, scoped by known system type, once in the user payload. The complete output catalog is not prompt context.
- Keep scientific comparison rows complete. Optional feedback shares context selection and records failures without changing calculation results; do not apply language-specific reply filtering.

## Heatmap Rules

- Two-dimensional grid sweeps may produce heatmaps.
- Heatmap specs use x and y for plane coordinates and color for the plotted numeric observable.
- Use a red-blue diverging colorbar with zero fixed as the white midpoint.
- Require at least two varying case variables and a numeric observable column before suggesting a heatmap.
- Require unique numeric x/y coordinates for one selected series; reject duplicates and unsupported grouping rather than overwrite or average rows implicitly.

# Molecular Hamiltonian Dataset Workflow

> Curated section: Planner.

> Plan and execute QH9-compatible molecular MD datasets through existing Study cases, then finalize, generate on the execution target, and explicitly collect.

## Executable Profile

- One seed molecule becomes one ordinary Study case running a complete NVE trajectory; sampled frames are dataset samples, not independent scheduler cases.
- Use neutral closed-shell H/C/N/O/F molecules, restricted B3LYP/def2-SVP, standard SCF, symmetry disabled, no density fitting, and no active-space/orbital-processing modules.
- Select executable qh9 for reference SCF conv_tol=1e-13, or qh9_relaxed_scf for conv_tol=1e-8. Both use conv_tol_grad=3.16e-5, grid_level=3, and diis_space=8. Registry settings apply through planning, validation and execution; explicit conflicting tolerances are rejected.
- Defaults are 100 molecules x 10 samples, NVE with 300 K initial velocities, time_step_au=50, steps=100, and zero-based frame indexes 9, 19, ..., 99. NVE is not thermostatted.
- Sampling is independent of SCF accuracy. For the QH9-dynamic-300k sampling schedule, explicitly select time_step_au=50, steps=100, sample_stride=1, sample_offset=0, and geometries_per_molecule=100 to keep every frame. The historical default keeps only ten frames.
- Preserve seed geometries, molecule/frame identities, coordinate units, and deterministic velocity seeds; retain initially unapproved Study resource review for all trajectory work.
- Molecular dynamics requires explicit molecular_dynamics.profile=qh9 or qh9_relaxed_scf. Dataset planning propagates the selected compatibility_profile; standalone or saved MD requests must select it before a new execution. Generic MD requests must not silently inherit QH9 scientific settings.

## Artifacts And Labels

- The task kernel owns trajectory execution and QH9-ordered Fock/overlap NPZ arrays. Compact manifests preserve AO permutation/phase/atom slices, sampled geometries and energies, units, array metadata, and convergence evidence.
- Integration failures preserve log-pyscf-output.log and result-molecular-md-failure.json with the failed frame, geometry, completed/retained frame counts, velocity seed, SCF convergence flag and last observed SCF residuals. Failed trajectories do not produce accepted frame arrays.
- For this RKS workflow, PySCF's Gradients did not converge message reflects the underlying SCF convergence flag. Inspect the saved log before choosing recovery; max_cycle can increase without relaxing conv_tol. Retry the complete trajectory in a new Run with the original molecule and velocity seed. Failure geometry is diagnostic evidence, not a supported MD restart checkpoint.
- Fock is a mean-field one-electron Hamiltonian label. It is not a full many-electron Hamiltonian; overlap and AO convention metadata must accompany it.

## Finalize, Generate, Collect

- Finalization writes samples.jsonl, rejections.jsonl, and dataset-manifest.json. Every expected frame must be accepted or rejected; rejected frames are not usable training samples.
- Remote finalization may use self-describing report metadata without opening or downloading executor-owned arrays. A metadata manifest does not prove local availability or validate remote file contents.
- generate_hamiltonian_dataset materializes and validates the portable dataset on the selected execution target, checks file presence/array keys/indexes/matrix shapes, rewrites relative matrix paths, and retains a generation receipt.
- collect_hamiltonian_dataset requires successful generation and downloads that dataset only when a local copy is requested. SSH generation returns only a lightweight receipt.
- Derive trajectory/sample progress and generated/collected states from the existing Study plan, receipts, and manifests; do not add another scheduler or mutable lifecycle.
- Neither dataset action requires content-checksum verification. Deployment source fingerprints are a separate concern.

## Splits And Evidence

- Default molecule_random splitting keeps all frames of a molecule together with train/validation/test fractions 0.8/0.1/0.1 and a persisted seed. geometry_random and molecule_size_ood require explicit selection.
- Record the selected profile, runtime PySCF and reference version 2.2.1, actual SCF setting deviations (empty for strict qh9), and bitwise_reproduction=false. Format/convention compatibility is not numerical reproduction.
- The 100 x 10 default is a plan. One-frame numerical smoke evidence does not establish full campaign quality, trajectory energy conservation, or downstream learning accuracy; require separate acceptance records.

pages.body:
# DMET Density Continuation And Branch Analysis

> Curated section: Planner.

> Compare qualified DMET candidates and prepare bounded density-only continuation sweeps with explicit provenance.

## Compare Saved States

- `analyze_dmet_branches(study_id, policy=None)` analyzes saved candidates without
  submitting calculations. Use final correlated sublattice charge and magnetic
  order, never the analytic seed name, to classify each converged state.
- Default order thresholds are 0.001 on absolute sublattice half-differences.
  A 20% threshold band is ambiguous; both orders give `mixed`, neither gives
  `near_unordered`, and unavailable observations give `unknown`. Record the
  configured policy with the analysis.
- Energy comparison requires successful execution, explicit convergence,
  passed required quality checks, and finite energy per site. Missing legacy
  quality evidence is unqualified; the optional density-fit residual is not a
  veto. Compare all indexed `candidate_runs`, including historical successful
  Runs after a failed retry. Current task rows and candidate minima differ.
- Energy ties default to 1e-6 per site. Order-magnitude differences above
  `state_tolerance=0.01` mark possible hysteresis; a sign reversal alone does not.
  AFM/CDW crossings require both branches at adjacent sampled V values. Do not
  bridge missing points or label numerical failure as a physical spinodal.

## Prepare And Start A Bounded Sweep

- `prepare_dmet_continuation` saves a preview and cost estimate;
  `start_dmet_continuation` starts that saved action through the existing Study
  retry lifecycle. Preserve cost-review requirements and the saved Study revision.
- Default `mode=bidirectional` follows AFM toward increasing V and CDW toward
  decreasing V at fixed U. `mode=nearest` uses scaled U/V distance and also
  supports mixed and near-unordered branches. Automatic selection requires
  uniform U/V, inline model specs, and compatible finite-graph DMET cases.
- Select the nearest qualified compatible donor again before each step,
  including newly completed and historical Runs. Each selected physical point
  and branch receives at most one new Run per action; equivalent seed cases are
  deduplicated. Missing donors cause a recorded skip, not an analytic fallback.
- Defaults are mixing 0.2, 200 outer iterations, outer DIIS off, bath policy
  `max`, and initial auxiliary correction zero. Repeated starts of one action
  do not resubmit. After interruption, collect existing Runs before preparing
  another action. A new action can revisit points while retaining candidates.
- FCI/CCSD DMET work/memory estimates are currently unavailable; missing
  estimates are not resource upper bounds.

## Density Transfer Contract

- `solver.options.reference_density_source` names a saved `source_case_id`,
  optionally an exact `source_run_id`, or a fixed absolute artifact path and
  SHA-256. The resolved donor is pinned to its Run and `dmet_mean_field_state`.
- Transfer the full final spin-resolved mean-field 1RDM, including off-diagonal
  entries. The target rebuilds its baseline with its own Hamiltonian and starts
  auxiliary u at zero. Correlation potential, chemical potential, DIIS history,
  and impurity wavefunction are not resumed.
- Check hash, source convergence/required quality, site basis, graph, fragments,
  spin/reference, bath and impurity settings. Only U/V may differ. Require real,
  finite Hermitian density of shape `(2,nsite,nsite)`, correct spin traces, and
  occupations in [0,1] within validation tolerance; never rescale the density.
- Old Runs without the final-density artifact cannot substitute initial seeds
  or correlated embedding densities. SSH stages local artifacts with checksum
  verification; cross-server paths must already be accessible to the receiver.

# Model Grid Convergence Barriers

> Curated section: Planner.

> Require converged, qualified model results before further sampling and coordinate saved Studies by absolute generation.

## Convergence Barrier Contract

- With `grid_refinement.require_converged`, every case must succeed, explicitly converge and pass required quality checks before more sampling. Optional `convergence_retry` allows one fallback per case; a failed fallback leaves `awaiting_convergence`. A shared `grid_round_target` advances only when all grouped Studies pass the current generation. These barriers do not change the solver or transfer a donor density.

## Sampling And Solver Choice

- Model studies use explicit solver settings under `study_mode=static`; optional
  `grid_refinement` adapts parameter sampling. This does not enable molecular
  initial-scan method routing or active-space selection.
- `grid_refinement.require_converged` requires every current case to have
  succeeded, explicitly converged, and passed required provider quality checks
  before generating further sampling points. Missing quality evidence blocks
  the barrier. Optional density-fit diagnostics do not independently block it.

## Bounded Convergence Retry

- Optional `convergence_retry` applies one numerical fallback per case, using
  the validated mixing, iteration limit and outer-DIIS settings. The recorded
  honeycomb policy uses mixing 0.1, 400 iterations and DIIS off; those study
  settings are not universal provider defaults.
- Persist fallback overrides before submission and use them during collection
  and interrupted-receipt recovery. Preserve the canonical sampling plan,
  analytic seed, case identity, actual execution requests and previous Runs.
- This fallback transfers neither donor density nor correlation potential.
  Density continuation is a separate planned action. An unsuccessful fallback
  leaves `awaiting_convergence`; do not generate later points or retry forever.

## Shared Generation Barrier

- The application `grid_group` coordinator uses normal saved Study services.
  An absolute `grid_round_target=0` permits only seed points; each additional
  generation permits one insertion batch. Restarting a generation must not
  resubmit completed tasks.
- Grant generation N+1 only when every member has passed generation N. A member
  that reaches its sampling/budget limit remains completed while others finish.
  Errors, interrupted workers and cancellation hold the group for inspection.
- Each Study retains its own coordinator, reports, receipts and candidate
  history; the group records barriers and runs no numerical calculations.
  Different studies may choose different refined coordinates after a barrier.
- The grid group is an application coordinator, not an independently exposed
  MCP numerical solver. Preserve the execution target and deployed runtime.

# Model Hamiltonian Input Contract

> Curated section: Model Hamiltonian.

> Model inputs are scientific artifacts that define structure, parameters, boundary conditions, and units.

## Required Fields

- model family such as Hubbard.
- dimension, preset, boundary condition, sites, bonds, and electron count.
- per-site onsite energy and Hubbard U when non-default.
- per-bond hopping integral t and Coulomb repulsion V when non-default.
- energy unit, written as `a.u.` when using atomic units.

## Template Metadata

- One-dimensional builder templates include chain, ring, zigzag chain, and quasi-1D ladder.
- Two-dimensional builder templates include square, Lieb, honeycomb, triangular, kagome, dice, and square-octagon.
- Template names are reproducibility metadata; execution must use exported sites, bonds, boundary condition, offsets, and parameters.
- Periodic templates must preserve image offsets and allowed sublattice connectivity.

## Must

- Treat the saved model input file as the source of structure truth.
- Store site and bond parameters explicitly when they differ from global defaults.
- Preview periodic bonds using boundary markers rather than drawing misleading direct in-cell connections.
- Keep solver choice outside the scientific model artifact.
- Preserve valid wrap bonds in small periodic cells even when the displayed source-target pair is already directly bonded.
- Display energy-like model parameters with the selected energy_unit wherever users inspect values.

## Must Not

- Do not store solver choice in builder output.
- Do not expose Holstein-Hubbard controls until an executable phonon solver and its validation/artifact contract are registered.
- Do not omit unit metadata from model parameters or energy outputs.
- Do not treat distance-only periodic completion as sufficient for decorated lattices such as dice.

# Model Hamiltonian Operations

> Curated section: Model Hamiltonian.

> Planner operations are controlled edits over a base model input.

## Target Fields

- Use site: 3 for one integer site ID and sites: [0, 2] for a list of integer site IDs. The shared operation engine applies grouped sites directly; splitting into single-site operations is unnecessary.
- A template reference in site must resolve to one integer; use sites for a reference that resolves to a group. A list in site is invalid and must not be flattened or reduced to its first element.
- Use bond: 7 for one bond ID, bonds: [2, 7] for bond IDs, and bond: [0, 2] for endpoint site IDs. Do not confuse site IDs with bond IDs.

## Allowed Operation Types

- `change_nelec`: change spin-resolved electron count.
- `set_site_parameter`: change onsite energy or Hubbard U on selected sites.
- `set_bond_parameter`: change hopping t or interaction V on selected bonds.
- `sweep`: produce cases over a numeric range.
- `case_design`: produce an explicit list of cases such as defects or dopings.

## Validation

- Reject unknown operation names.
- Reject site or bond indices not present in the input file.
- Reject ambiguous parameter names.
- Normalize electron-count operations before case generation.
- Use capability-registry parameter scopes to decide whether a parameter is valid for site, bond, global, or sweep usage.

# Model Hamiltonian Electron Count Contract

> Curated section: Model Hamiltonian.

> `nelec` must be spin-resolved before execution.

## Rule

- `nelec` at execution boundary must be a two-item list or tuple: `[nalpha, nbeta]`.
- For total electron count N: if N is even, use `[N/2, N/2]`; if N is odd, use `[(N+1)/2, (N-1)/2]` unless the user specifies spin differently.
- Validate `0 <= nalpha <= norb` and `0 <= nbeta <= norb`.

## Must Not

- Do not pass scalar total electron counts to `change_nelec`.
- Do not infer high-spin alternatives unless the user asks for them.
- Do not execute if electron count exceeds orbital capacity.

## Failure Example

- Bad: `{"op":"change_nelec","nelec":3}`.
- Good: `{"op":"change_nelec","nelec":[2,1]}`.

# Builder Navigation and Messaging Contract

> Curated section: Model Hamiltonian.

> Builder navigation is a UI/browser handoff protocol, not a scientific model schema.

## Message Schema

- Builder save messages must include target, work directory, saved input path, and lightweight model metadata for UI preview.
- Target identifies whether the receiver is the single agent or planner agent.
- Caller surfaces must update their model input state from the returned path.

## Navigation Rule

- Open builder in a named window or tab when caller state must be preserved.
- Back-to-web-UI actions must notify the opener instead of reloading and losing state.
- If the opener is unavailable, show the saved path and let the user manually return.

## Must Not

- Do not use download-only builder output for agent integration.
- Do not route planner builder output to the single-agent state or vice versa.
- Do not refresh the agent/planner page on return.

- [[Model Hamiltonian Input Contract]]
- [[Model Hamiltonian Builder State Loss]]

pages.summary: PySCF documentation and source examples expand the agent's scientific context,
pages.body:
# PySCF Reference Capability Boundary

> Curated section: PySCF Methods.

## Rule

PySCF documentation and source examples expand the agent's scientific context,
but they do not expand what it can execute. `PlatformRegistry` plus backend
validation are the only execution authority.

## Implemented Agent Surface

- Molecular HF, DFT, MP2, CCSD, CCSD(T), FCI, CASCI, CASSCF, and
  ground-state SC-NEVPT2 under its CAS restrictions.
- Molecular correlation diagnostics: frontier gap/degeneracy, natural
  occupations when available, T2 and CCSD T1/D1 evidence, opt-in SCF stability, and
  an auditable active-space proposal.
- Molecular SCF density fitting and restricted/ROHF DF-CASSCF with FCI or
  block2 (`scf_and_casscf`), Boys/Pipek-Mezey localization summaries,
  fixed-block localization plus canonical/Fiedler/manual orbital ordering for
  approved block2 CASCI/CASSCF, molecular structure preview, and a curated common
  basis-set list.
- Finite Hubbard model MP2, CCSD, CCSD(T), FCI, unrestricted-reference
  diagnostics, and finite-cluster FCI observables; plus primitive-cell one-body
  Bloch tight binding with band, DOS, filling, and Hamiltonian artifacts.
- Optional libDMET ground-state DMET for Builder-defined single-band Hubbard
  finite clusters, including translated and explicit finite-graph fragments,
  restricted or broken-symmetry UHF (`Sz=0`) references, FCI/CCSD/block2 DMRG
  impurity solvers, bounded self-consistency, and structured result/history/numerical
  artifacts.
- Static molecular/model scans and adaptive molecular scans, plan-scoped active-space approval, case-local
  recovery, result merge, restart-safe case checkpoints, plot-data artifacts,
  and explicit resource-review gates for expensive FCI/CAS or tensor-scaled
  plans.
- Molecular FCI/CASCI/CASSCF targeted roots within the configured sector,
  including same-sector state-averaged CASSCF. Targeted roots are not a complete
  spectrum and do not enable excited-root SC-NEVPT2.
- Molecular `job=molecular_dynamics` with the registered `qh9` (SCF 1e-13)
  or `qh9_relaxed_scf` (1e-8) profile: restricted B3LYP/def2-SVP NVE trajectories for neutral closed-shell
  H/C/N/O/F molecules. One trajectory is one Task; sampled coordinates,
  energies, Fock and overlap arrays are artifacts. This is not a general MD
  engine, optimizer, or mid-trajectory continuation interface.
- AVAS AO/atom-fragment projection with retained spin-adapted CAS initial
  orbitals after active-space approval.
- Optional block2 fixed-orbital DMRG-CASCI and single-state or same-spin/symmetry-
  sector state-averaged DMRG-CASSCF for
  restricted/ROHF molecular active spaces, plus finite-model targeted-root DMRG
  with structured sweep, RDM, orbital-ordering, and checkpoint-manifest
  artifacts. Molecular and model runs share a result/recovery contract.
  DMRG-CASSCF uses PySCF macroiterations with internal MPS
  continuation and preserves optimized orbitals plus solver traces. Compatible
  cross-task DMRG-CASSCF runs can restore optimized orbitals and MPS jointly.
  Exact fixed-particle-number Schmidt-rank caps, bounded bond-dimension
  escalation, and heuristic error estimates are
  available. Entanglement/occupation evidence may propose an unapproved
  expanded ActiveSpaceAudit that restores only optimized orbitals and starts a
  fresh MPS. Explicit
  result analysis tracks targeted roots from root 1RDM/natural-occupation
  signatures and may propose an approved same-executor retry from a compatible
  state-trusted successful MPS; ordinary initial cases remain independent.
- Single periodic HF/DFT tasks for 3D POSCAR or CIF cells. ASE expands CIF
  symmetry to an explicit P1 cell. The contract includes gamma-centered or
  Monkhorst-Pack meshes, shifts, FFT/auxiliary cutoffs, PBC density fitting,
  exact-exchange divergence, occupation smearing, and structured
  structure/numerics/orbital artifacts. Optional automatic or validated custom
  high-symmetry mean-field bands use analysis k points separate from the SCF
  sampling mesh and write Fermi-referenced JSON/TSV artifacts. SeeK-path mode
  additionally standardizes to the HPKOT primitive cell, executes on that
  effective cell, and preserves input/effective structures plus a full
  transformation audit. Charged, spin-polarized, or unrestricted-reference
  supercell reductions are blocked because input-cell electron counts and
  broken-symmetry magnetic periodicity cannot be inferred safely.
- Optional restricted periodic G0W0, approval-gated HF+DMFT, and staged
  GW+DMFT through the fcDMFT provider. These are single-task workflows with
  registered native artifacts; GW/DMFT total energies are not fabricated when
  the provider does not expose them.

## Roadmap Or Reference Only

- Different-spin state averaging, unrestricted DMRG-CASSCF, transition-RDM or
  direct-wavefunction root tracking, ab initio DMET including DMRG impurities, AFQMC,
  SHCI, MCPDFT,
  MRPT, and other external
  solver interfaces.
- Periodic Planner scans, ab-initio DOS, forces/stress, cell optimization, and
  periodic MP2/CC or unrestricted GW/DMFT.
- Interacting Bloch-model solvers and Bloch adaptive routing; the current
  tight-binding solver records but does not apply `U/V`.
- Different-spin state averaging and state-specific excited-state orbital
  optimization outside the registered targeted-root/state-average routes,
  and excited-root SC-NEVPT2.
- Standalone gradient/Hessian tasks, geometry optimization, solvent, QM/MM,
  general dynamics beyond the registered QH9 trajectory profile,
  electron-phonon solvers, GPU workflows, and forge extensions.

## Promotion Requirement

A roadmap capability becomes executable only after it has a structured contract,
backend adapter, registry entry, validation, artifact schema, UI surface where
needed, bounded cost behavior, and regression tests.

## Must Not

- Do not construct runnable plans from a PySCF API name alone.
- Do not call a design-only builder field an executable backend capability.
- Do not infer that a basis listed in PySCF documentation has been individually
  curated for UI selection; the backend accepts safe names separately.

- [[Capability Registry]]
- [[Planner Workflow Validation]]
- [[Molecular Method Selection Rules]]
- [[Strong Correlation Roadmap Rules]]

# PySCF Reference Core API Rules

> Curated section: PySCF Methods.

## Scope

This document summarizes core PySCF API rules from the local PySCF source wiki
and user guide wiki. It is a reference page for code generation and future
backend work; it does not expand current agent execution capability.

## Source Coverage

- Source wiki pages: `StreamObject Protocol`, `Mole Input Contract`, `Cell Input
  Contract`, `Method Factory Selection`, `Kernel Return and State Pitfalls`.
- User guide chunks: `usage-model`, `molecule-gto`, `crystal-cell`, `scf`.

## Rules

- PySCF inputs are usually Python scripts or Python objects, not a separate
  input-file language.
- Molecular workflows start from `pyscf.gto.Mole`, `gto.M(...)`, or
  `pyscf.M(...)`.
- Periodic workflows start from `pyscf.pbc.gto.Cell`, `pyscf.pbc.gto.M(...)`, or
  compatible `pyscf.M(a=...)` patterns.
- Use module-level factory functions such as `scf.RHF(mol)`, `dft.RKS(mol)`,
  `mp.MP2(mf)`, `cc.CCSD(mf)`, and `mcscf.CASSCF(mf, ncas, nelecas)`.
- Existing PySCF objects may expose convenience methods through dynamic
  dispatch, such as `mol.RHF()`, `mol.KS(xc='pbe')`, `mol.CCSD()`, and
  `mol.CASSCF(6, 6)`.
- `.kernel()` returns the method's main result and is not type-uniform across
  modules.
- `.run()` calls `.kernel()` and returns the object, which is safer when later
  code must read attributes such as `e_tot`, `e_corr`, `mo_coeff`, `mo_occ`, or
  `converged`.

## Implemented Agent Boundary

- The current molecular backend may generate and execute molecular HF, DFT,
  MP2, CCSD, CCSD(T), FCI, CASCI, and CASSCF through its own task-spec and
  execution layer.
- The periodic backend executes 3D gamma-point or regular-k-mesh HF/DFT from a
  dedicated periodic task contract. It does not reuse molecular `Mole` input.
- The current model-Hamiltonian backend does not execute arbitrary PySCF
  scripts from the reference wiki; it consumes normalized model specifications.
- Periodic occupation smearing and ASE automatic, SeeK-path standardized, or
  validated custom mean-field band paths are executable through dedicated
  structured contracts. Optional fcDMFT contracts execute restricted periodic
  G0W0, approval-gated HF+DMFT, and staged GW+DMFT without exposing arbitrary
  PySCF post-HF calls. Periodic MP2/CC, force/stress, and cell optimization
  remain reference or roadmap material.

## Must Not

- Do not assume a PySCF object method is available just because a dynamic method
  name looks plausible.
- Do not mix molecular `Mole` and periodic `Cell` APIs unless a source-backed
  conversion helper is intentionally used.
- Do not expose `.kernel()` return values as stable structured results without
  normalizing them through backend code.

## Related Pages

- [[Task Specification Contract]]
- [[PySCF Reference Capability Boundary]]
- [[PySCF Roadmap Periodic Calculations]]

pages.body:
# Molecular Method Selection Rules

> Curated section: PySCF Methods.

> Molecular calculations must use normalized method, reference, charge, and spin settings.

## Capability Matrix

- `hf`: Hartree-Fock; omit `xc`; validate RHF/UHF/ROHF reference.
- `dft`: density functional theory; require `xc`; validate RKS/UKS reference.
- `mp2`: post-HF method requiring a converged HF reference.
- `ccsd`: coupled-cluster method requiring a compatible HF reference.
- `ccsd_t`: CCSD plus perturbative triples for a weak single-reference regime.
- `fci`: Full CI using orbitals from mean-field setup; prefer small systems by default.
- `casci` and `casscf`: approved active-space methods; SC-NEVPT2 is a restricted ground-state post-CAS correction.

## Method Rules

- Hartree-Fock is represented as `hf` and must omit `xc`; non-DFT methods normalize empty `xc` to null.
- DFT requires an exchange-correlation functional such as B3LYP.
- Post-Hartree-Fock methods require a valid mean-field reference.
- MP2, CC, CI, FCI, and CAS must be validated against closed-shell/open-shell support.
- CASSCF/CASCI require explicit approved ncas/nelecas; do not silently choose an ambiguous active space.
- Explicit molecular density fitting supports scf_and_casscf for restricted/ROHF CASSCF with FCI or block2; legacy scf scope on restricted CASSCF normalizes to that combined scope. Results report actual applied_to and the optimizer implementation. Unrestricted DF-CASSCF and DF active two-electron integrals in block2 CASCI are unsupported.
- block2 CAS defaults solver.options.mpo_algorithm to conventional; fast_bipartite remains an explicit option and saved explicit selections are retained. Conventional uses NC for two orbitals and defaults integral_cutoff to 1e-12 (FastBipartite: 1e-20). This integral-screening threshold differs from DMRG truncation cutoff. Effective settings and MPO/sweep/RDM timings are recorded. Small fixed-orbital checks against FCI and official dmrgscf/block2main pass. The lutein M=600 Amarel comparison observed about 55% lower custom-process peak RSS and only 2.3% shorter median time with Conventional over two repeats; all paths remained unconverged. This does not establish a general speedup. Active-space Boys/PM supports explicit orbital_processing.localization_occupation_thresholds: [] preserves whole-block localization, [1.0] separates low/high reference occupations, and [0.1, 1.9] defines three groups. Diagonalize the spin-summed SCF density projected into the selected active block, then localize each interval independently; no 2-RDM is required. Boundaries are strictly increasing inside (0,2), with equality in the lower interval. Record occupations, group membership and preserved-subspace checks in cas_result.orbital_provenance. Fiedler ordering is separate. This changes only the initial orbital basis, not active-space membership or subsequent CASSCF rotations; compatible joint restarts retain their saved basis. In the lutein fixed-CAS(20e,20o), M=600 pilot, whole PM+Fiedler and split PM+Fiedler both met DMRG criteria while whole PM without reordering did not. Whole PM+Fiedler was slightly lower in energy and faster in that single comparison; keep split localization optional and do not infer CASSCF orbital convergence from this fixed-orbital result.
- MolecularCorrelationRisk preserves separate physics, solver-stress, overall diagnostic, and routing levels. Nonconvergence raises the overall diagnostic warning without rewriting physical evidence; solver stress alone need not trigger multireference promotion.
- T1 >= 0.05 or D1 >= 0.10 is the current CCSD policy threshold for multireference review, not a universal accuracy cutoff. Ground-state SC-NEVPT2 requires an approved spin-adapted CAS and root 0.
- Restricted/ROHF CASSCF with FCI or block2 accepts orbital_processing.frozen_orbital_indices (default []). These are reviewed, unique zero-based full MO indices after active-space preparation, recorded in cas_result.orbital_optimization. Explicitly frozen external virtuals are omitted from the internal MO integral workspace; all occupied and active MOs remain with their requested PySCF frozen constraints. Checkpoints and output arrays restore the complete MO layout, and integral_space records the working-to-full mapping. AO integrals and J/K operations retain the full AO basis. Freezing holds orbital coefficients fixed without reducing the AO basis or changing the CAS electron count. Inactive double occupancy alone is not orbital freezing. No automatic chemical-core count or virtual-energy cutoff is assumed.

## Reference Rules

- Ordinary closed-shell single-reference methods default to restricted references. Automatic CAS uses a UHF orbital probe followed by shared spatial orbitals and spin-adapted RHF/ROHF CAS; initial_reference and cas_reference are distinct.
- Open-shell systems default to unrestricted or ROHF only when supported by the selected method.
- A user-provided reference override wins after validation.
- Model Hamiltonian mean-field-based solvers default to unrestricted references; do not apply the molecular closed-shell default to half-filled model systems.

## Must Not

- Do not leave stale DFT defaults when the user switches to Hartree-Fock.
- Do not run post-HF without a compatible mean-field object.
- Do not let UI method labels diverge from the normalized backend task spec.

## Validated Lutein Boundary (September 21)

- The September 20–21 lutein follow-up achieved converged M=600 orbital optimization with PM+Fiedler and Conventional MPO. A separate fixed-orbital M=2000 solve does not establish M=2000-optimized CASSCF. With 42 frozen core orbitals, the full external-space result shifted by 0.0248 mHa from the preceding unfrozen result. Initial +3/+5 eV external virtual windows failed the agreed 0.1 mHa energy and 0.01 NOON-difference targets despite inner/orbital convergence. Compressed and original MO workspaces agreed within 8e-10 Ha at the same frozen constraints. These are case-specific observations, not automatic core/window defaults. AO DF storage remains full-size, so fewer working MOs do not imply proportionally lower peak RSS. See the September 21 overnight-results report.

- [[Correlation Diagnostic Interpretation]]
